mechanism: Both drugs inhibit monoamine oxidase (rasagiline is a selective MAO-B inhibitor, isoniazid is a weak non-selective MAO inhibitor), creating additive risk of hypertensive crisis and serotonin syndrome when combined with sympathomimetic amines or serotonergic agents.
action: Avoid concurrent use if possible; if combination is necessary, monitor closely for hypertensive episodes, headache, chest pain, and serotonergic symptoms; counsel patient on dietary tyramine restriction and avoid sympathomimetic medications.
